doc.title: Winard Harper interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 10, 2014

title: Best gigs: playing with heroes from his wall
summary: Harper says no gig was the worst, recalls Max Roach's phone calls, and plays tonight with Dick Hyman.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Again, this is sometimes a hard question. What’s the best gig or series of gigs you ever had, and on the other hand what might have been the worst?

I don’t know if I can ever say I’ve had a worst. I mean all the gigs I’ve had have been important and great to me. Because I’m still a fan of the music. You know what I mean? Every time I can still get on the bandstand with those guys that I have posted on my wall, you know, I have the album covers tacked up or I had read the interviews or you know what I mean? For me to have them still be around and call me up. Wow. You know what I mean? Like sometimes like when Max would call me up. Like wow. I actually remember sitting in that bedroom as a kid hearing my first Max Roach-Clifford Brown record. You know what I mean? So I mean when I can talk to him on the phone and he’ll call my name it’s like — it’s being a part of something. Being accepted you know. Having the stamp of approval. At the same time I had so much respect for him. Even sometimes they would call me up for gigs I would still light up like somebody else was getting a big gift for, you know, Christmas day or something. It’s like wow.
Nice. That’s a great sentiment. Playing with those guys that were on the wall.

I mean even tonight because still I always think about Dick Hyman. Dick Hyman’s in that Charlie Parker video. You know what I mean? One of the few videos of Charlie Parker and he had the chance to sit there with Charlie Parker. Tonight I’ll be sitting with him. I mean I’m a history buff so all those things are always — you’re grateful.

I totally agree. Like Bucky. He’ll just say something in passing. “Oh that thing I did with Paul McCartney recently” or, like what? It was so much their day to day, they got on this level and it was always good. © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-
